newsitem.title: UK: Bomb under Sinn Fein car defused in N.Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Bomb under Sinn Fein car defused in N.Ireland.

text.p: British army experts defused a booby-trap bomb planted under the car of a local Sinn Fein councillor at Ballycastle north of Belfast, police said on Friday.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for planting the device but Protestant Loyalists, who want Northern Ireland to stay British, were under suspicion, they said.
The device was planted days after Sinn Fein's guerrilla sympathisers, the Irish Republican Army, killed two policeman in an attack that jolted faltering Northern Ireland peace efforts.
The IRA says it is fighting to end British rule of Northern Ireland to reunite it with the predominantly Roman Catholic Irish republic.
The car's owner, James McCarry, said he noticed the device when he checked it on Thursday afternoon. "It appeared to be a booby-trapped device. There was a magnet and wires," he told reporters.

Loyalists, so-called because of allegiance to Britain, are supposed to be observing a ceasefire since October 1994 but a series of attacks on Irish nationalist and Catholic targets in recent weeks have been blamed on them.
